phase_name: Entry Guards That Mechanically Refuse a Deferred Unfiltered Battery

objectives.description: verify-deploy.sh entry guard, reserved exit 3, --override-batch-gate-deferral flag
run-all.sh parallel entry guard, reserved exit 3, --override-batch-gate-deferral flag
orchestrate-batch-gate.sh passes the override on both deploy_findings_snapshot calls
7 new test cases (refusal/scoped/nested/guest/stale/override/absent) in test-batch-gate-pending-marker.sh; fixed a now-broken assumption in test-gate-registry-resolution.sh

approaches_tried.approach: Warning call nested inside the is_pending true-branch
approaches_tried.reason: A stale/malformed marker is by definition never 'pending', so nesting the warning call inside that branch makes it unreachable -- caught by Case 11's own second assertion. Moved to print unconditionally, before the pending check.

notes: Scope Hypothesis confirmed live: exactly 3 real gate-acquire call sites exist (run-all.sh's own top-level bracket, plus verify-deploy.sh's gate8_run and gate31_run), but only 2 TOP-LEVEL entry points need a guard -- gate8_run/gate31_run's acquires are both downstream of verify-deploy.sh's single top-level guard and never reached if it refuses first.

A test-authoring bug (a stray duplicate run-all.sh invocation that ran before its marker was seeded) hung the new suite against the REAL repository's own full 209-suite battery; found via bash -x tracing and fixed. No real harm (no mutation, just wall-clock cost), but recorded since it is exactly the risk class this body of work is about.

test-verify-deploy-gate-selection.sh (29/0) and test-verify-deploy-gate-selection-crash-net.sh (1/1, auto-discovering and cleanly running all 31 registered gates including the new gate 31) both re-run green with no changes needed -- both are registry-driven and absorbed the new gate automatically.

test-gate-registry-resolution.sh's own case32 broke: it runs '--only-gate <live max>' for REAL as a cheap acceptance probe, an assumption that held while the live max was a fast lint (gate 30) and silently stopped holding once gate 31 (the slow-bucket gate this phase's sibling Phase 2 created) became the new max -- the probe then ran the real 10-15-minute slow battery. Fixed by adding --skip-slow (gate-agnostic no-op for every gate but 8/31) and relaxing the case's own exit-code assertion to check the ABSENCE of the out-of-range rejection text instead of a bare 'rc -eq 0' (a --skip-slow selection whose only gate defers entirely trips the pre-existing, unrelated zero-check-under-filter guard, exit 2 -- a different exit-2 cause than an out-of-range rejection, now told apart by message text). Added to this task's declared file_scope and landed in the same follow-up commit as the other Phase 5 work.
